title: Optimizing GPU performance (Crusoe Cloud docs)
quote: To reduce clock switching latency and ensure that the maximum SM clock is available across all execution kernels
proves: A rented-GPU cloud documents running nvidia-smi -lgc (with sudo, after sudo nvidia-smi -pm 1) on its VMs, so clock locking is possible on at least some rented VM instances.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about containers (RunPod/Vast/Colab) or about locking to low clocks; page does not state root policy explicitly.
bearing: C9 feasibility: rented VM with root can lock clocks

title: cuda.bindings.nvml device_set_gpu_locked_clocks (NVIDIA cuda-python docs)
quote: Requires root/admin permissions.
proves: Locking GPU clocks via NVML (what nvidia-smi -lgc calls) needs root and is supported on Volta or newer.
does_not_prove: Does not say which clouds grant it; Colab and container providers unverified.
bearing: C9 feasibility blocker: no root, no clock lock

title: The economics of speculative decoding (Fergus Finn blog)
quote: Any number of speculation tokens makes MLA immediately compute bound!
proves: Roofline analysis for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on B200: weights GEMM crosses the fp8 ridge at about 281 tokens per step, but MLA attention (kept in bf16) is compute-bound from the first speculated token (T=2).
does_not_prove: Analytic, not measured; B200 not H100; MLA only (GQA attention intensity is far lower); no clock or energy data.
bearing: C9: spec raises attention intensity in a way batch does not; where clock sensitivity should appear

title: The roofline model for LLM inference: are you compute bound or memory bound (Spheron blog)
quote: 989.5 TFLOPS / 3.35 TB/s ≈ 295 FLOPs/byte
proves: H100 SXM ridge is ~295 FLOP/byte bf16 (~591 fp8); bf16 decode needs ~280 tokens per step to cross it, so (K+1)*B must reach ~280 before the weights matmul is compute-bound at full clock.
does_not_prove: Spec-sheet arithmetic only; ignores KV traffic and that peak FLOPs scale with SM clock (ridge in tokens roughly halves at half clock); not measured.
bearing: C9: ridge point for judging where clock sensitivity appears

title: Characterization of Request and Token Energy Costs for LLM Inference Workloads on GPU Platforms
quote: We evaluate this LLM inference energy model on NVIDIA H100 and H200 GPUs across dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models
proves: Recent (Aug 2026) H100/H200 energy characterization decomposing request energy into fixed prefill/setup cost plus marginal per-token energy across batch, context, output length.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculative decoding, clock frequency or power caps.
bearing: C9 gap evidence: datacenter energy studies still omit spec

title: The Joule Point: an Energy-Optimal Operating Point for AI Inference
quote: The minimum, which we name the Joule Point, is a cap at 43 to 46 per cent of a large GPU's rated power
proves: Dense power-cap dataset (ELF, 20 models, 4 GPUs) finds an energy-optimal cap at 43-46% of rated power cutting energy per inference by about a quarter to a third.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculative decoding or SM clock locking; does not show whether spec moves the Joule Point.
bearing: C9: baseline power-cap optimum without spec; competing knob

title: DualScale: Energy-Efficient Disaggregated LLM Serving via Phase-Aware Placement and DVFS
quote: DualScale dynamically adapts GPU frequency per iteration using stage-specific control
proves: Per-iteration GPU DVFS for decode is already built on a 16x H100 cluster (Llama 3.3 70B), up to 48% decode energy cut vs DistServe.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculative decoding; whether its decode controller models K+1-token verify steps is unknown.
bearing: C9 adjacent: per-step DVFS primitive exists; spec would be an input

title: HyperKuvid-Labs/energy_throttling_llms (GitHub)
quote: A cookbook, not a paper
proves: Hobby repo sweeps SGLang EAGLE3 steps/topk/draft tokens per batch (1-16) on an RTX 4060 laptop GPU using power telemetry to keep avg power at 95-98% of an 80 W limit; 8B gain within noise.
does_not_prove: Does not set clocks or power limits; laptop GPU; no energy-optimal clock result; no paper.
bearing: C9 scoop (weak): energy-aware K tuning by telemetry

title: FASER: Fine-Grained Phase Management for Speculative Decoding in Dynamic LLM Serving
quote: FASER minimizes computational waste by dynamically adjusting the speculative length for each request
proves: Per-request speculative length in continuous batching plus draft/verify spatial multiplexing in vLLM; up to 53% throughput, 1.92x lower latency.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention energy, power, clocks or quantized kernels; whether its cost model is online or offline unknown.
bearing: C9/C10: adaptive K under load already exists without energy or drift

title: IST-DASLab/marlin (GitHub README)
quote: enabling the maximum possible 3.87x speedup up to batchsizes around 16-32
proves: FP16xINT4 Marlin keeps near-ideal 4x weight-read speedup only up to ~16-32 tokens per matmul; beyond that compute per 4-bit weight exceeds the GPU FLOP:byte budget, so INT4 shifts the ridge to ~4x fewer tokens than bf16.
does_not_prove: No numbers at 64/128 tokens in text; not a spec study.
bearing: C8: INT4 verify at (K+1)*B >= 16-32 loses the quantization advantage; predicted by roofline

title: AutoAWQ README (casper-hansen/AutoAWQ)
quote: 20% faster than GEMM, only batch size 1 (not good for large context).
proves: AWQ ships separate GEMV (batch 1 only) and GEMM kernels; GEMV is marked avoid at batch 8. Repo deprecated and archived May 11, 2025.
does_not_prove: No spec measurement; kernel-choice guidance only.
bearing: C8: the 1-token vs multi-token kernel split is long known

title: Speculative Decoding Meets Quantization: Compatibility Evaluation and Hierarchical Framework Design
quote: verifying a tree-style draft incurs significantly more time overhead than a single-token forward pass
proves: On A100 with vLLM Marlin W4A16 kernels, EAGLE-2 tree verification (tree 60) costs 1.8x a decode step vs <1.2 for FP16/W8A8; proposes a hierarchical small intermediate model to turn trees into sequence drafts; 2.78x on 4-bit Llama-3-70B, 1.31x over EAGLE-2.
does_not_prove: Does not choose tree size from hardware cost (uses EAGLE-2 defaults; sweeps tree size on A100 and 3090); batch size not stated (framed as single-batch); no Apple/Metal.
bearing: C8 novelty: the quantized-verify tax on GPUs is published and a remedy proposed

title: [Performance] qmv kernel: non-linear cost step at M=3 for large MLP shapes (ml-explore/mlx #3553)
quote: speculative decoding verify passes (draft_length=2 produces M=3)
proves: On M4 Pro 4-bit, qmv cost jumps at M=3 for MLP shapes (13824->5120: 0.277 ms M=1 to 0.379 M=3, 0.477 M=4); Qwen3.6-27B full model 68.0 ms M=1 vs 93.8 ms M=3; reproduced on M1 Pro and M3 Max. Closed Aug 5 2026 after qmv_wide kernels.
does_not_prove: Single-op microbenchmarks; no end-to-end spec speedup or K choice; M5 not measured.
bearing: C8: MLX kernel community already tracks verify-width cost

title: Add a BM=16 qmm tile for the small-M decode dead-zone (ml-explore/mlx PR #3863)
quote: deliberately does **not** touch the `qmv_wide` slope where single-stream speculative-decode verify (M = 2–6) lives
proves: On M3 Max, get_qmv_batch_limit returns 10 for 5120x17408; qmm at M 10-16 sits on a 0.51 ms plateau, a BM=16 tile gives 1.63-1.68x. Closed unmerged Aug 2 2026; maintainer says small-M relies on qmv_wide.
does_not_prove: Not merged; only one machine; does not measure spec end to end.
bearing: C8: cost curve vs M is non-smooth and kernel-specific; being engineered upstream

title: 2-bit quantized_matmul loses its size advantage over 4-bit at M >= 3 (ml-explore/mlx #3852)
quote: each extra row costs about 45% of the whole M=1 call
proves: M4 Pro mlx 0.32.0: 2-bit is 1.6x faster than 4-bit at M=1 but equal at M=3; 2-bit cost vs own M=1 is 1.82x at M=3, 4.53x at M=8; author sees ~1.2x spec speedup on 2-bit 27B vs 1.6-2.1x on 8-bit. Closed Aug 16 2026, maintainer declined to optimize.
does_not_prove: Author hypothesis that marginal row is compute-bound is not proven; one machine; spec numbers anecdotal.
bearing: C8: lower-bit targets pay a larger verify tax on Apple; also C10: marginal rows may be clock-sensitive

title: mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp (main)
quote: if (M >= 2 && use_qmv_wide(mode, d) && !global_scale) {
proves: MLX main dispatches M>=2 to qmv_wide (affine mode on arch gen >= 15) and switches to qmm/qmm_splitk at a per-shape, per-GPU-generation vector_limit (e.g. 33/25/13 on gen 17+ non-d parts).
does_not_prove: Current main, not the pinned MLX 0.32.1 on the Air; does not give timings.
bearing: C8: the verify-width cost curve on Metal is set by a shape-dependent dispatch table

title: llama.cpp release b11404 (newreleases.io mirror)
quote: so DFlash2 decoding on an M3 Ultra was slower than serial decoding.
proves: llama.cpp Metal added few-row MMA mat-mul kernels for 2..16 src1 rows that dequantize each weight once for all rows, gated by thresholds (F32 6; F16/Q4_K/Q5_0/Q5_1 3; others 2) tuned on M3 Ultra, to fix spec verify that was slower than serial.
does_not_prove: Mirror page, exact date not shown (pre-release, ~2026); no end-to-end spec numbers.
bearing: C8: the serial-verify bug on quantized Metal is being fixed by kernel engineering

title: Adaptive speculative decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: computes the batch average, smooths it with an exponential moving average (EMA)
proves: SGLang adapts speculative_num_steps at runtime per batch-size tier from an EMA of acceptance length only (EAGLE/EAGLE3, topk 1), re-deciding every 5 verify batches.
does_not_prove: Docs mention no measured step-latency or cost input, so cost drift (thermal, clocks) is not tracked.
bearing: C10/C9: shipped adaptive K ignores cost drift

title: The Gap Is the Loop: What Background Work Really Costs On-Device LLM Decode on Apple Silicon
quote: a synchronous loop leaves the GPU idle for about 6% each step while the submitting CPU core downclocks
proves: On a base M4 batch-1 8B decode, a synchronous loop idles the GPU ~6% per step as the CPU core downclocks; pipelining removes 95% of the gap (+9-12%); bandwidth contention slows decode up to 72%.
does_not_prove: No thermal throttling and no spec decode; abstract only.
bearing: C10: on Apple silicon, CPU DVFS and contention move step cost, not only GPU thermals; vllm-metal spec needs sync scheduling

title: Your MacBook is fast for two minutes, then half as fast (llmconfigurator guide)
quote: minute 10:  19.8 tok/s
proves: Shows a minute-1 42.6 tok/s vs minute-10 19.8 tok/s example and says fanless Airs throttle hardest.
does_not_prove: Unnamed model and machine, no method; Air vs Pro claims are explicitly not measurements.
bearing: C10: throttling magnitude on Macs is anecdotal; no draft/verify split
